//: Glacier · FROST. One hue, navy to ice, over a painting: a blue-haired figure
//1: on an ice throne, ice swords, snowflakes, stars. No upstream palette — every
//2: role is lifted from the picture, and `tokens` names each after what it is
//3: there so the mapping stays traceable. THE source for every shell surface
//4: (quickshell/: bar, launcher, OSD, power menu); theme.lua still owns WINDOW
//5: chrome (gaps, border, blur, shadow) and CI cross-checks it against this.
//6: Two-tone rule, cold edition: ICE CYAN (the swords) is the frame, WHITE (the
//7: cap) is the readout, PALE CYAN (the near-white ice) is the launcher. Warm
//8: never appears on the shell at all: the painting has no yellow and no green,
//8a: so `warn` is the VIOLET in the ice shadows (do-not-disturb, the dirty dot,
//8b: the mid step of every ramp) and `ok` is LIT ICE (a charging bolt, a ramp's
//8c: cool end) — state read as a shift in the one hue, not a foreign one. Only
//8d: `urgent` leaves it, as a cold rose. The terminal keeps a real ANSI yellow
//8e: and green (wezterm/colors.lua) because ls and git mean something by them.
//9: readoutBright is declared, so the active workspace
//10: is an emissive white -> ice lozenge (see modules/Workspaces.qml), a lit
//11: snowflake rather than a solid block. Frost is structural, not a color: the
//12: islands sit at 0.55 so the painting shows through Hyprland's blur, and the
//13: only glow is a quiet cyan one.
name: glacier
//tokens: What in the painting -> role, so a palette bump stays traceable. urgent has no token: it is state, not scenery.
//effects: Cold glow: text glows in ice cyan, wider and quieter than cyberpunk's neon (10px, low alpha everywhere it is used). The panel texture is a sheen — a catch light along the top edge of every pane and a white wash under it, gone by mid-height — light on ice, not a raster. 0.2 over the resting 0.12: the islands sit at 0.55 over bright blurred ice, and a quieter sheen vanished into it.
//bar: Bar identity. Frosted glass: the islands are the most translucent of any theme (0.55 — the painting shows through, blurred by the layer rule), a thin 1px ice hairline at 35%, 12px corners, and a faint cyan bloom (0.22 over 20px) that reads as cold light on ice rather than neon. No accent line. The fill is a navy a shade UNDER `ground`, not `surface`: the top of the painting is bright ice and sky, and at 45% show-through a deep-ice fill composited to a mid blue that the quiet type could not sit on (`dormant` 2.6:1, `urgent` 3.0:1 over the picture's average; 2.3:1 and 2.7:1 over the strip the bar actually covers). The darker fill lands the composite at ~#264469 — `dormant` 3.1:1, `urgent` 3.6:1, `text` 8.5:1 — with the frost untouched.
//launcher: Launcher identity: a pale-cyan 1px frame around frosted glass (0.62), 12px window, 8px input + rows.
//osd: OSD identity: a frosted pill — 1px ice-cyan frame, white track, 0.7 so the wallpaper still shows under the frost.
//session: Power-menu identity: 12px frosted tiles with a 1px ice edge at 50%, over a 0.6 navy scrim — the lightest backdrop of the dark themes, so the throne stays visible behind the menu.
//wallpaper: Shared by hyprlock.conf (brightness) and sddm/Main.qml (1 - brightness scrim). 0.5 with a 10px blur: the picture is already bright ice, and the lock screen is where the figure is actually seen (the desktop keeps her under the windows), so it is dimmed a touch further than the other dark themes and frosted harder.
